items.title: LRT line hits construction milestone; route will link Mississauga and Toronto
items.summary: Work on a major light-rail transit line being built in east Mississauga and Toronto hit a “critical milestone” this week with the completion of an important underground task, project leaders say. “Crews have completed tunnelling on the 500-metre twin tunnels that will run between Jane Street and Mount Dennis Station (in Toronto) and connect the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension to Line 5 Eglinton,” Metrolinx, the provincial transit agency working with Infrastructure Ontario to build the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension, said in a project update on Monday. The underground work began in February and took some six months to complete. 2-kilometre above ground/underground route will extend the Eglinton Crosstown LRT line in Toronto, also known as Line 5 Eglinton, farther west to “bring much-needed rapid transit to Etobicoke and Mississauga,” project officials have said. When completed, the ECWE will help reduce gridlock and connect nearly 70,000 commuters to jobs across the Greater Toronto Area, the provincial government said earlier. The new LRT line is also expected to extend from the Mississauga-Toronto border north to Toronto Pearson Airport in Mississauga. Work crews break through the final section to complete the second tunnel. (Photo: Metrolinx) Ontario Premier Doug Ford said earlier this summer that as the GTA continues to grow, “our government is making historic investments in the largest public transit expansion in North America to support commuters, fight gridlock and protect workers.

items.summary: A 52-year-old Mississauga man has been charged in connection with an ongoing child luring investigation involving youths under the age of 16. items.title: Mississauga fall recreation programs now open for registration
items.summary: Register for swimming, first aid, leadership and preschool programs. Mississauga is offering swimming and aquatic leadership programs this fall. Mississauga residents can now browse and register for the city’s fall recreation programs through Active Mississauga. In-person registration is also available at community centres during service desk hours. Nonresident registration opened Aug. m. Swim for Life lessons help participants build swimming and water-safety skills through step-by-step instruction for different ages and skill levels. The courses provide youth and young adults with a pathway toward careers in aquatics and recreation, including lifeguarding, swim instruction and aquatic leadership. Participants will develop leadership and teamwork skills. A new Intermediate First Aid (CPR-C & AED) course is available this fall. Formerly known as Standard First Aid, the course provides training to help participants respond to a various range of emergencies, including allergic reactions, strokes, burns, fractures, seizures, diabetic emergencies and environmental injuries. The course also includes CPR-C and AED certification, a prerequisite for Bronze Cross. The city is offering a variety of preschool programs guided by the HIGH FIVE® quality standard.

Appointment of President and Chief Executive Officer The Board of Directors is pleased to announce the appointment of Jocelyne Moyer as the President and Chief Executive Officer of Next Hydrogen and its subsidiaries and a director of the Company effective September 1, 2026. As previously announced, Raveel Afzaal, will transition from the CEO role and leave the board as of August 31, 2026. Ms. Moyer holds a Bachelor of Engineering and Management in Mechanical Engineering from McMaster University and a Master of Business Administration from Harvard Business School. She began her career in front line plant and operations management and in supply chain optimization with major companies including Maple Leaf Foods and PepsiCo. She also worked from 2016 to 2022 at Bain & Company advising senior executive teams of industry leading companies on critical strategic issues. Ms. Moyer joined Heliolytics in 2022 as Director of Strategy and Operations and became General Manager in 2023, shortly before its acquisition by Zeitview.

items.title: 141 New Units Proposed for Three Modular Towers on Ninth Line in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the City of Mississauga is reviewing a proposal from Mattamy Homes for three modular six-storey apartment buildings at 6344 Ninth Line, just south of Doug Leavens Boulevard. Mississauga.com reports the three towers would together add 141 units to the site. The application asks the city to change the zoning bylaw currently in place so the development can go ahead. According to the report, the proposal also includes additional landscape and public realm enhancements planned around the perimeter of the property. Mississauga.com notes a public meeting on the application has been scheduled for September 21, giving residents a chance to weigh in before the city makes a decision.

Installing a pool, building a deck or removing a tree that’s in the way? Before you begin, check whether you need a tree permit. Trees on both private and public property are protected under the City’s tree protection by-laws. Updated in 2022, the by-laws ensure trees in Mississauga are managed responsibly. As Mississauga experiences hotter summers and more extreme weather, protecting the urban forest helps keep neighbourhoods cooler, healthier and more resilient.

items.title: New bylaw better protects renters from unlawful renovictions in Mississauga
items.summary: New rules aimed at better protecting renters in Mississauga will be in place in two weeks. The City of Mississauga’s Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing Bylaw, to take effect Sept. 1, will prevent tenants from being unjustly evicted by landlords who say they’re planning major repairs to the property — a practice known as renovictions. Adopted by city council in April, the new bylaw “increases protections for tenants who face eviction when their landlord requires them to move out for extensive renovations or repairs,” city officials said earlier. The city noted on Monday the bylaw, which works in tandem with the Ontario Residential Tenancies Act to better protect renters from unlawful renovictions, was developed with input from tenants, landlords and community groups across Mississauga. “These changes will help make the eviction process clearer and fairer, while reducing housing instability and helping protect the city’s supply of affordable rental housing,” officials said. Renovictions have become more common in recent years, prompting Mississauga municipal politicians to take action in defence of city renters.
